safety_evidence.result: An additional spot (Rf 0.01) appeared in the Shodhana milk, indicating the transfer of chemical constituents from Raktagunja seeds into the processing medium during detoxification.

results.result: No time- or dose-dependent lethality up to 10 mg/ml confirming absence of cytotoxicity and safety at tested dose.
Decreased crystallite size and peak broadening confirm nanocrystalline transformation, indicating improved bioavailability compared to raw mica.
Transformation of biotite mica with formation of iron-oxide–rich and amorphous phases confirming physicochemical modification during processing linked to antimicrobial activity.

Detection of stable crystalline phases in the entire formulation such as cinnabar (HgS), sulphur, cassiterite (SnO₂), orpiment (As₂S₃) and mica confirms conversion of toxic metals into stable sulphide/oxide mineral forms and long-term chemical stability.

The formulation contains stable crystalline phases such as cinnabar (HgS), cassiterite (SnO₂), massicot (PbO) and magnetite (Fe₃O₄) confirmed with identical patterns across batches, indicating stable, transformed and intact mineral forms supporting safety and stability of bhasma-based formulation.
Metals present only as stable oxides/sulphides (Fe₂O₃ major phase; SnO₂, HgS, SiO₂, HgO minor phases) confirming safe chemical transformation of toxic metals into non-reactive forms.

ICP-AES of the entire formulation confirms the presence of therapeutically important elements (Hg, S, Fe, Sn, Au, Cu, Ca, Mg etc.) with heavy metals (Cd, Pb, As) within permissible limits confirms controlled composition and safety.

In the firmulation the essential and trace elements (Mg, Cu, B, Mn, Al etc.) detected in controlled therapeutic ranges without abnormal accumulation, confirming safe elemental composition and proper transformation of mineral ingredients.
Appearance of organo-metallic bonds and reduction of impurity-related bands demonstrate chemical detoxification and enhanced biological compatibility.
High thermal stability with minimal weight loss confirms removal of volatile impurities and formation of a stable product.
Formation of stable metal-oxide bonds confirms structural modification into a more therapeutically active and stable form.
Homogeneous micro-to-nano particle distribution (majority 0.5–2 µm) confirming high dispersion, reduced toxicity risk and improved biological compatibility of Bhasma-based formulation.
Reduction in toxic aluminum content and formation of organo-metallic complexes indicate detoxification and improved safety.
Presence of 50-500 nm nanoparticles confirms nanosizing, enhancing pharmacological efficacy and systemic availability.
Increased surface area and porosity suggest enhanced dissolution and better therapeutic performance.
Majority of particles in nano range confirms uniform particle size distribution, improving absorption and consistency.
High iron with presence of antimicrobial trace metals (Zn, Mn, Cu, Sr, Pb) confirming release of antimicrobial cations contributing to antibacterial activity.

Toxic heavy metals (Pb, Cd, As, Hg, Cr) were quantitatively estimated in the entire formulation and found within permissible safety limits, confirming absence of hazardous heavy-metal toxicity in the formulation.
Majority of particles present in the formulation (Mahalaxmivilas Rasa) was in micro-range (3.46–210 µm) confirming particle size reduction and improved dissolution and gastrointestinal absorption.
Significant reduction in CFU and absorbance against S. aureus and MRSA confirming antibacterial efficacy of laboratory-prepared Abhraka Bhasma against Gram-positive bacteria.
Formation of stable metal-oxide bonds confirms structural modification into a more therapeutically active and stable form.
Moderate CEC values confirming ability to release bioactive cations in aqueous medium enhancing antimicrobial action.
No color change observed indicating absence of free elemental metals, confirming detoxification and safety of the Bhasma and final formulation.
